advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm revision-only artifact dedup cannot collapse two distinct Gerrit changes that share the same commit SHA (cherry-pick / dual-push), or restore a change-scoped component to the match.
evidence: Prior key was the full title `code-review: {change_id} @ {revision}` (voter.py:288), i.e. (change_id, revision); new key is revision-only.

Vote-dedup still keys on the distinct change_ids (src/rebar/review_bot/voter.py:512 `key = (change_id, revision)`, :708 `store.record_vote(change_id, revision, ...)`), so two same-SHA changes both vote but the artifact collapses to one.
advisory.finding: Artifact idempotency now keys purely on the `revision` string (via `existing_title.endswith(f" @ {revision}")`), dropping the change_id component of the prior exact-title match. Two DISTINCT Gerrit changes sharing an identical commit SHA (e.g. a cherry-pick preserving the tree, or the same commit pushed as two changes) would be collapsed into one artifact, so only the first change gets the artifact and its trailer `relates_to` links while the second change's votes still occur but produce no artifact.
scenarios: A commit is cherry-picked with `-x` (or force-pushed) such that two separate Gerrit changes reference the identical revision SHA
A submodule/monorepo flow that pushes one commit object to two review changes

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide whether alias-replay should re-emit a REVIEW_RESULT with a differing change_id/change_fingerprint, or normalize to the artifact's canonical change identity before emit.
evidence: src/rebar/review_bot/voter.py:287: `change_fp = sidecar.change_fingerprint(change_id, revision, changed_files, diff_text or "")`
src/rebar/llm/code_review/sidecar.py:51: `"change_id": change_id or "",` (fingerprint basis includes change_id → alias yields a different fp)
src/rebar/review_bot/voter.py:318-324: emit is called with change_id/revision/change_fp on every invocation, including the reuse path
src/rebar/review_bot/voter.py:309-311: the create-time description embeds `change_id` and is not updated on reuse
sidecar.py:124-127: emit docstring states idempotency 'is not attempted here … callers emit once per produced verdict'
advisory.finding: On alias replay the existing artifact is reused, but `sidecar.emit` is still called with the replaying alias's `change_id` and a recomputed `change_fp` (which differs because change_fingerprint incorporates change_id), appending a second REVIEW_RESULT payload whose `change_id`/`change_fingerprint` no longer match the reused artifact's title or its first sidecar; the artifact's description (written once at create time) also continues to name only the first change_id.
scenarios: A rerun via the compact `rebar~986` alias after the initial webhook review with the canonical `I…` id — the reused artifact accumulates a REVIEW_RESULT payload tagged with a change_id/fingerprint that disagree with its title

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a get_change_event case with a payload missing `change_id` asserting the event id falls back to the REST `id`.
evidence: tests/unit/test_review_bot.py:787-799 — the sole test payload always includes both `id` and `change_id`, so only the first branch of the ladder is exercised
ABSENCE: no test supplies a ChangeInfo payload lacking `change_id` to assert the fallback to `d.get('id')`
advisory.finding: The new fallback ladder in get_change_event (`d.get('change_id') or d.get('id') or change_id`) is only tested for the tier-1 case (change_id present). The tier-2 fallback (change_id absent → use the REST `id`) introduced/reordered by this diff has no test; a regression dropping `or d.get('id')` would go undetected.
scenarios: A Gerrit change payload omits `change_id` (older/limited REST response); the intended fallback to the REST id must fire.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a parametrized case (or second test) where the mocked _get_json returns a dict with `id` but no `change_id`, asserting event['change']['id'] == 'rebar~986'.
